content_units: Uneven Mini-Split Cooling in Your Berlin Apartment

A bedroom that gets very cold while the living room stays warm usually points to an airflow, sizing, control, or refrigerant-distribution issue rather than just dirty filters. With a 6-year-old outdoor unit and a budget of about   €250   for the visit, the best goal is to do basic homeowner checks first, then call for a diagnostic-focused service visit if the imbalance remains.
Home Troubleshooting and Likely Cause Ranking
Step   Action   What to Check   Expected Result
1   Compare indoor unit settings   All heads in   Cool   mode; similar temp setpoints; fan not on extra-low in living room   Rooms should respond more evenly
2   Check louvers and airflow   Living-room vanes open; no curtains, shelves, or furniture blocking intake/discharge   Strong, steady cold airflow from living-room head
3   Inspect temperature conditions   Close windows/doors; note sun exposure, cooking heat, electronics, occupancy in living room   Confirms whether heat load is much higher there
4   Test fan speed   Set living-room unit to   High   fan for 15–20 min   Better throw and improved room pull-down
5   Listen for abnormal behavior   Clicking, gurgling, short cycling, weak fan, delayed start, ice, or water leaks   Helps separate control vs refrigeration faults
6   Check condensate and coil signs   No ice on indoor coil/piping; drain flowing normally; no musty blockage signs   Rules out freeze-up or airflow restriction
7   Observe outdoor unit   Coil visibly clear; fan runs smoothly; no loud buzzing/vibration; free airflow around condenser   Outdoor unit should reject heat normally
8   Record a simple temperature split   Measure room temp and supply-air temp at each head after 15 min in Cool mode   Big difference between heads suggests system imbalance/fault
Most likely causes, ranked
Option 1:   Living-room airflow or setup issue     Most common when one room cools and another does not   Check louvers, fan speed, blocked return/discharge, incorrect mode
DIY check
Option 2:   Living room has much higher heat load     Large windows, afternoon sun, kitchen gain, electronics, occupancy can overwhelm that zone   Especially likely in a larger open-plan living area
Heat-gain tips
Option 3:   Low refrigerant charge or distribution problem     One head may still cool while another underperforms, especially under load   Needs technician gauges and leak check
Service info

Option 4:   Indoor unit fan, coil, or sensor issue in the living room     Weak blower, dirty blower wheel/coil, bad thermistor, or control board issue   Common if airflow feels weak despite clean filters
Option 5:   System sizing or design limitation     120 m² can be a lot for a mini-split layout if living room is the dominant load   More likely if problem appears during hot sunny hours only
Option 6:   Outdoor unit performance decline     At 6 years old, capacitor, fan, or coil-condition problems can reduce capacity   Possible, but usually affects whole system, not just one room
What to Collect Before You Call the HVAC Technician
Have this ready so the technician can diagnose quickly within your    €250   visit budget:
-   System details
- Brand and model numbers of outdoor unit and each indoor head
- Approximate installation year
- Whether it is single-zone or multi-split
-   Symptom pattern
- When the living room stays warm: all day, only afternoons, only on hotter days
- Whether the bedroom is always too cold or only after long runtime
- Any recent change from previous summers
-   Basic measurements
- Room temperature in bedroom and living room
- Supply-air temperature at each indoor unit after 15 minutes in Cool mode
- Outdoor temperature at the time of test
-   Operating settings
- Mode, setpoint, fan speed, swing/louver position for each indoor unit
- Whether units are running simultaneously
-   Visible/ audible signs
- Ice, leaks, unusual noise, weak airflow, odors, short cycling
- Outdoor fan running or not
- Error lights or fault codes on remotes/indoor units
-   Maintenance history
- Filters cleaned last week
- Any prior refrigerant top-up, leak repair, coil cleaning, or PCB/fan repairs
Fast measurement method
- Run all active heads in   Cool  , set to   20–22°C  , fan   High  , for   15–20 minutes  .
- Use a simple thermometer at:
- center of each room
- 5–10 cm from each unit’s discharge air
- Note sun exposure and whether kitchen appliances were used.
Best Use of a €250 Service Visit
Ask for a   diagnostic-first appointment  , not an open-ended repair visit.
Recommended scope for the first call:
- Confirm airflow and control settings at each indoor unit
- Measure temperature split at each head
- Check refrigerant pressures / performance
- Inspect indoor coil, blower wheel, thermistors, and condensate
- Inspect outdoor coil, fan operation, and electrical condition
- Quote repair separately if leak search, parts, or refrigerant work is needed
Good outcome for this budget:
- Full diagnostic
- Minor cleaning/adjustment
- Written findings with repair estimate
Potentially outside this budget:
- Refrigerant leak search and repair
- Refrigerant recharge
- Fan motor, thermistor, PCB, or valve replacement
- Deep coil/blower disassembly cleaning
